name: Takayama / Hida
tagline: A mountain merchant town: Hida beef, miso on a leaf, new sake and morning markets.
history: Takayama sits in a high, snowy basin in the Alps, cut off for centuries. In 1692 the shogunate took the region for itself, for its timber and mines, and the town became a centre of rich merchants, famous carpenters and sake breweries. The Sanmachi streets still keep the houses from that time.

The morning markets go back to the Edo period, near the Takayama Betsuin temple. Today's market on the Miyagawa riverbank has run since 1953, and the one in front of the Jinya completes the pair. They sell pickled Hida red turnip, apples, miso, mochi and dango.

Hida beef is black Wagyu fattened in Gifu for at least 14 months, with a quality grade of 3 or more. The bull Yasufuku, bought from Hyogo (Tajima line) in 1981, sired about 39,000 offspring and made the brand. It has had geographical-indication status since 2023.

The cold explains the rest: hōba-miso, miso with spring onion and mushroom grilled on a dried magnolia leaf over a burner, comes from the winter habit of warming miso on a leaf over the irori. The local mitarashi (みだらし) is dango with soy sauce only, savoury, without Tokyo's sweet syrup.
winter: Snow, and new sake (shinshu) at the breweries, marked by the green cedar ball (sugidama) that browns as the sake matures. Hōba-miso at ryokan breakfast. In the last days of the year the Miyagawa market becomes the 'toshinose' market, with New Year decorations and hanamochi.

meibutsu.name: Hida beef
meibutsu.what: Gifu Wagyu: as steak, sukiyaki, yakiniku or grilled on hōba-miso.
meibutsu.where: Steak House Kitchen Hida, Shuntei Nakagawa, Bourbon. Mark Wiens spent 24 hours eating Hida beef (Kyōya, Maruaki and others).
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: well done, and skip the raw egg with sukiyaki.
meibutsu.glance: Gifu's black Wagyu: as steak, sukiyaki or grilled on miso.
meibutsu.story: One bull made this brand. In 1981 a bull called Yasufuku was bought from Hyōgo, of the Tajima line, and he sired about 39,000 offspring. Hida beef is black Wagyu fattened in Gifu for at least 14 months and graded 3 or above; since 2023 it has had geographical-indication status. Have it as steak, sukiyaki or grilled on hōba-miso. For Fernanda: well done, and no raw egg.

meibutsu.name: Hida beef nigiri
meibutsu.what: A slice of seared beef over rice, sold at the Sanmachi stalls. Not on any Tabelog list.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: Rare meat. Fernanda skips it; the others can have it for the photo.
meibutsu.glance: A seared beef slice over rice; a Sanmachi street-stall photo.

meibutsu.name: Hōba-miso
meibutsu.what: Miso with spring onion and mushroom grilled on a magnolia leaf on a table burner, eaten with rice. Sometimes topped with Hida beef.
meibutsu.where: Ryokan breakfast; Kyōya (Mark Wiens had the beef version); the markets sell kits.
meibutsu.glance: Miso and mushrooms grilled on a magnolia leaf, eaten with rice.
meibutsu.story: Takayama sits in a high, snowy basin, and this dish comes from the cold: people used to warm miso on a leaf over the irori, the sunken hearth. Today it arrives on a small table burner: miso with spring onion and mushroom on a dried magnolia leaf, sometimes topped with Hida beef. Let it bubble, then scoop it onto your rice. Ryokan breakfasts serve it, and the markets sell kits.

meibutsu.name: Takayama ramen
meibutsu.what: Light soy broth, thin wavy noodles. Born at a street stall in 1938.
meibutsu.where: Masago Soba (the 元祖). Mark Wiens tried Tsuzumi.
meibutsu.glance: Light soy broth with thin wavy noodles, born at a 1938 stall.
meibutsu.story: Takayama ramen began at a street stall in 1938, and Tabelog reviewers still call Masago Soba, the stall that became a shop, the original. Locally it's called chūka soba. Expect a light soy-sauce broth and thin, wavy noodles, and a bill under ¥1,000. Masago has tables of four, so we sit 4+3. Mark Wiens tried another shop, Tsuzumi. Slurp the noodles while they're hot.

meibutsu.name: Hida mitarashi dango
meibutsu.what: Rice balls on a skewer, grilled and brushed with soy sauce only. Savoury, not sweet.
meibutsu.glance: Grilled rice dumplings on a skewer, brushed with soy only.
meibutsu.story: Tokyo's mitarashi dango comes in a sweet syrup. Takayama's doesn't: here it even has its own name, midarashi, and it's brushed with soy sauce only, so it's savoury. Rice balls on a skewer are grilled and glazed with soy. Buy them hot at the morning-market stalls or at Jinya Dango, about ¥100 a skewer (to confirm), and eat them while they're warm.

meibutsu.name: Pickled red turnip
meibutsu.what: Hida red turnip, pickled: crunchy and sour. A market classic.
meibutsu.glance: Crunchy, sour pickled red turnip; a morning-market classic.

meibutsu.name: Sanmachi new sake
meibutsu.what: In Dec–Jan the Sanmachi breweries are brewing and pour tastings of the new sake.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: Alcohol. For Fernanda: kōji amazake (alcohol-free); the kind made from sake lees (sakekasu) contains alcohol.
meibutsu.glance: New-season sake poured at the Sanmachi breweries in winter.

meibutsu.name: Shōjin ryōri
meibutsu.what: Vegetarian temple cooking: tofu and mountain vegetables.
meibutsu.glance: Vegetarian temple cooking: tofu and mountain vegetables.

areas.name: Miyagawa Morning Market
areas.story: About 50–70 stalls on the riverbank since 1953, heirs to the Edo markets.
areas.tips: In winter many stalls start at 7:00; open until ~12:00. Heavy snow can cancel it.
areas.dec_jan: On the Takayama alternative (28–30 Dec) our market mornings are Tue 29 Dec and early on the 30th before we leave: the year-end 'toshinose' market, with New Year decorations. Whether it runs 1–3 Jan (to confirm) doesn't affect us.
areas.glance: Riverside morning market since 1953: pickles, dango, miso, apples.

areas.name: Jinya-mae Market
areas.story: A smaller market in front of the shogunate's old government house.
areas.tips: Pair it with Miyagawa the same morning.
areas.glance: A small morning market by the shogunate's old government house.

areas.name: Sanmachi
areas.story: Streets of merchant houses and breweries with a sugidama over the door.
areas.tips: Very busy at midday; go early. The nigiri stalls are a tourist showcase.
areas.dec_jan: Brewery tastings over 29 Dec–3 Jan to confirm; for us that's 29 Dec only.
areas.glance: Old merchant streets with breweries under green cedar balls.

places.name: Steak House Kitchen Hida

tabelog.awards: ステーキ EAST 百名店 2025

places.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: well done; the kitchen is happy to do it.
places.group: 24 seats at tables; book for seven.
places.dec_jan: Lunch and dinner; closed Wednesdays (30 Dec, our leaving day), so dinner on Mon 28 or Tue 29 Dec. Year-end hours to confirm.
places.glance: The Hida beef steakhouse Japanese diners trust.

places.booking: Online, with a strict cancellation fee.

places.dec_jan: Closed Sundays, which doesn't touch 28–30 Dec. Year-end hours to confirm.
places.glance: An izakaya of Hida home cooking, with tatami rooms.

places.glance: The 1938 original of light, soy-broth Takayama ramen.

places.dec_jan: Closed Wednesdays (30 Dec), so 28 or 29 Dec. Year-end hours to confirm.

shops.buy: The meat counter is for looking; the restaurant is the meal.

shops.name: Sanmachi breweries

shops.buy: Bottles of new sake; kōji amazake for Fernanda.
shops.dec_jan: Year-end tastings to confirm; 29 Dec is our day for them.
